title: Expedia Uses AI-Driven Service Telemetry Analyzer to Accelerate Incident Investigation
gist: Expedia Group built Service Telemetry Analyzer (STAR), an internal AI-assisted observability platform that explicitly rejects autonomous agents in favour of a deterministic prompt-chaining workflow: it pulls Kubernetes and JVM infrastructure metrics from Datadog, runs domain-specific prompts, and emits a consolidated root-cause report that engineers must review before acting. The current build deliberately uses no function calling, RAG, memory or autonomous tool use, and moved from FastAPI background tasks to Celery on Redis because telemetry and LLM calls are I/O bound and rate-limited.

themes.theme: Deterministic workflow chosen over autonomous agents

insights.claim: Expedia Group's Service Telemetry Analyzer deliberately avoids autonomous AI agents in favour of a deterministic workflow — telemetry collected, analyzed with domain-specific prompts, consolidated into intermediate findings, then summarized into a final report of potential root causes and recommended next steps.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Another large enterprise landing on deterministic pipelines over agent loops for incident response — the pattern is now the mainstream production choice, not the conservative one.
insights.quote: Rather than adopting autonomous AI agents, the platform follows a deterministic workflow in which telemetry is collected, analyzed using domain-specific prompts, consolidated into intermediate findings, and summarized into a final report

insights.claim: Expedia states that the current STAR implementation uses none of function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, memory, or autonomous tool use, relying purely on predefined workflows specifically to generate consistent analyses.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A production AI system shipping without the entire fashionable feature set — evidence that consistency, not capability, is the binding constraint in operational AI.
insights.quote: Expedia said the current implementation does not use capabilities such as function calling, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), memory, or autonomous tool use, instead relying on predefined workflows to generate consistent analyses.
insights.locator: 'The platform is implemented as a FastAPI application'

insights.claim: The stated objective for STAR is to minimize time to know (TTK) and time to recover (TTR), making incident-duration metrics rather than diagnostic accuracy the platform's declared success criterion.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: TTK/TTR are the ROI metrics AI observability tooling will be judged on — the frame to demand from any vendor pitching AIOps.
insights.quote: Our objective with this service was to minimize the time to know (TTK) and time to recover (TTR).
insights.locator: 'Describing the project's goal, the team wrote'

insights.claim: STAR is implemented as a FastAPI application that integrates with Datadog for service metrics and with an internal generative AI gateway that centralises authentication and access to LLM providers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The internal-AI-gateway pattern — one controlled chokepoint between apps and LLM providers — is becoming standard enterprise architecture and a distinct product category.
insights.quote: The platform is implemented as a FastAPI application that integrates with Datadog to retrieve service metrics and an internal generative AI gateway that manages authentication and access to LLM providers.

insights.claim: Expedia replaced FastAPI background tasks with a Celery-based asynchronous architecture using Redis as both message broker and result backend, driven by the fact that most STAR processing is I/O bound telemetry retrieval and LLM requests.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: LLM-backed internal tooling hits queueing-architecture problems, not model problems, as it scales — the engineering cost that vendor demos never surface.
insights.quote: The engineering team states that most processing consists of I/O bound operations involving telemetry retrieval and LLM requests.

insights.claim: The asynchronous execution model exists to let STAR process multiple analysis tasks concurrently while accommodating rate limits imposed both by Datadog and by Expedia's own internal AI gateway — the two upstream quotas that bound throughput.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Observability-vendor API rate limits are an unpriced constraint on enterprise AI incident tooling — a hidden lever in Datadog-class contract negotiations.
insights.quote: The asynchronous execution model allows STAR to process multiple analysis tasks concurrently while accommodating rate limits imposed by Datadog and the company's internal AI gateway.
insights.locator: 'The engineering team states that most processing'

themes.theme: Infrastructure telemetry as the polyglot lingua franca

insights.claim: STAR restricts itself to standardized infrastructure telemetry from Kubernetes-based services and JVM applications precisely because infrastructure metrics provide a consistent view across services written in different programming languages and frameworks.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Standardising the input schema — not enriching it — is what makes an AI diagnostic pipeline generalise across a polyglot estate; a design rule worth copying.
insights.quote: Expedia explains that infrastructure metrics provide a consistent view across services developed using different programming languages and frameworks.

insights.claim: The specific metric set STAR analyses is request throughput, latency, HTTP, gRPC and GraphQL error rates, CPU and memory utilization, container restart events, Kubernetes readiness and liveness probe failures, Java heap utilization, and garbage collection activity.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A concrete, bounded feature set is what an LLM RCA harness actually needs — useful as a checklist against which to test 'full-stack AI observability' claims.
insights.locator: 'The system analyzes metrics including request throughput'

themes.theme: Human-in-the-loop and how quality is actually measured

insights.claim: Engineers review STAR's generated findings before acting on any recommendation, which Expedia describes as making the platform an assistive tool rather than an autonomous operational system — humans retain validation and decision-making responsibility.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Even the enterprises furthest along in AI incident response are not automating action — the autonomous-remediation market is smaller and later than vendor narratives imply.
insights.quote: Engineers review the generated findings before acting on recommendations, making the platform an assistive tool rather than an autonomous operational system.
insights.locator: 'The company reports that STAR has been used'

insights.claim: STAR has been used in real production incident investigations, post-incident analysis, Kubernetes troubleshooting and JVM memory diagnostics — four distinct workloads, indicating it is past pilot stage.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Post-incident analysis and memory diagnostics are lower-risk entry points than live incident response — the sequencing most enterprises will follow.
insights.locator: 'The company reports that STAR has been used'

insights.claim: Prompt management, tracing and evaluation for STAR run through Langfuse, while overall system performance is assessed via subject matter expert reviews and user feedback rather than an automated benchmark.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Even a production LLM observability system has no quantitative eval — the missing measurement layer is the current gap and the opportunity in AI-ops tooling.
insights.quote: Prompt management, tracing, and evaluation are currently supported through Langfuse, while system performance is assessed using subject matter expert reviews and user feedback.

themes.theme: Roadmap: where the deterministic design gets loosened

insights.claim: Planned STAR enhancements include incorporating service dependency information, additional operational metadata, Model Context Protocol based tool integrations, and conversational interfaces — meaning the deliberately tool-free design is slated to acquire tool access via MCP.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: MCP is entering enterprise observability roadmaps as the standard tool-integration layer — watch adoption there as a leading indicator for the protocol's durability.
insights.quote: Planned enhancements include incorporating service dependency information, additional operational metadata, Model Context Protocol (MCP) based tool integrations, and conversational interfaces.
insights.locator: 'The blog also describes ongoing work to expand the platform'

insights.claim: Expedia is evaluating STAR as part of its chaos engineering practice to help analyze the results of controlled failure experiments, extending an incident-response tool into pre-production resilience testing.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Chaos-experiment analysis is a natural second market for AI RCA tooling — the same harness, with ground truth available for evaluation.
insights.quote: Expedia is also evaluating STAR as part of its chaos engineering practices to help analyze the results of controlled failure experiments.
